fact: NCRA's May 2024 presentation lists among its technology assets an upgraded integrated eCRVS System for the registration of birth, death, marriage, divorce and adoption events; it does not say where or by which offices the entry is made.

The National Civil Registration Authority, the state agency formed under the 2016 Act, presents the integrated eCRVS and ID management system as its own, with data held in its own Tier III data centre, in May 2024.

NCRA states that since the launch of its electronic registration and securitised certificate system over 200,000 citizens and residents have had births, adoptions, marriages, divorces and deaths registered and linked digitally to its identity management system; no denominator is given.

fact: The CRVS and ID management system is described as managed by the NCRA, the authority created by the 2016 law that consolidated registration of vital events and identity management in one entity; a live birth registration on it was demonstrated at 34 Military Hospital, Freetown.

NCRA's Director General says the modern integrated CRVS system was developed with European Union support through UNOPS, and thanks UNDP, UNICEF, UNFPA, the EU and Irish Aid for supporting the integration and digitisation; no domestic funding is stated.

fact: NCRA's own page says that, although a pilot civil registration ran between March and June 2017, it is yet to establish the civil registration system that will cover births, deaths, marriages, divorce, adoption and nullities, and that permanent registration centres beyond the districts are yet to be set up; the page is undated and the date is its published year.

The National Civil Registration Act 2016 (law on 30 June 2016) establishes NCRA and gives it the registration of births, deaths, marriages, divorces and adoptions, taking births and deaths from the National Office for Births and Deaths and marriages and divorces from the Administrator and Registrar General.

In the third and fourth quarters of 2017 UNDP contracted PricewaterhouseCoopers to develop a roadmap for a comprehensive CRVS system, producing a governance structure, a Strategic Plan, an ICT roadmap and policies and procedures for registration, archiving and sharing of vital events; the page gives the plan no end date.

fact: The National Civil Registration Act 2016 (section 2, sections 15 and 37) establishes the National Civil Registration Authority as a body corporate responsible for registering births, deaths, marriages, divorces, nullities and adoptions throughout Sierra Leone, and requires it to establish and maintain the electronic Integrated National Civil Registration System.

Section 21 of the Act provides in law that the Authority is financed by moneys appropriated by Parliament, together with gifts, grants and other contributions and other moneys accruing to it; this is the statutory provision, with no amount stated.

The Act provides in law (sections 37 and 42) that the Integrated National Civil Registration System creates and maintains the civil status registers in electronic format, the registers including a Register of Births and a Register of Deaths; a statutory provision, not a report of practice.

The Act provides in law (sections 37(3) and 38(3) to (5)) that the system functions at national, regional, district, chiefdom and ward levels, that data are entered once at the place where the event occurs, and that local registration centres send their data regularly to the districts for transmission to regional or national level; section 34 keeps a manual Personal Registration File alongside the electronic entry. A statutory provision, not a report of practice.

The EU's 2021-2027 indicative programme for Sierra Leone names support to an integrated civil registration information system as a governance priority, with expected result 2.2 that an Integrated National Civil Registration Information System is established and accessible at local, district and national level for the registration of vital events (baseline registration rates birth 78%, death 16%; targets 95% and 90%); no amount is given for it, and the date is the document's published date.
system: Integrated National Civil Registration Information System
